description:
Found in defk-9p6.14 (PCM mixing). Summing n equal-length streams that arrive concatenated in one [i16] (m = div(len(bufs), n)) is the dominant cost of the mix kernel, and every form of the inner loop keeps a bounds check, so clang does not vectorise it (0.75 ns per element, ~70% of the kernel at 1 s chunks; the clamp loop next to it, check-free, vectorises at width 8).

Minimal repro (report: :full):

    defk add_blocks(bufs :: [i16], n :: i64) :: [i64] do
      m = div(len(bufs), n)
      sums = alloc(i64, m)
      for j <- 0..(n - 1)//1 do
        base = max(j * m, 0)
        for i <- 0..(min(len(sums), len(bufs) - base) - 1)//1 do
          sums[i] = sums[i] + bufs[base + i]   # bufs[base + i]: bounds check kept; nothing proves base + i < len(bufs)
        end
      end
      sums
    end

0 <= base is proven (max with 0) and sums[i] is check-free, but i <= len(bufs) - base - 1 does not give base + i < len(bufs): offsets are only tracked for literals. The shifted form has the same gap from the other side:

    for i <- m..(min(len(acc), len(bufs)) - 1)//1 do
      acc[i] = acc[i - m] + bufs[i]          # acc[i - m]: nothing proves 0 <= i - m
    end

(the range start m is not carried as a lower bound of i). Related: defk-9za (facts from a guarding if), defk-pic (alloc length facts).

Done when: both loops compile with no bounds check, in both modes, with a test; examples/pcm_mix.exs can then drop the check from its sum loop (expected: the loop vectorises).

title: Prove b[base + i] in bounds for a variable block offset (i <- 0..(len(b) - base - 1), or i <- m..(len(b) - 1) with b[i - m])
